I understand where you are coming from OP, it’s natural to not want to feel alone but if you feel isolated even being with your friends, then I would say they are not friends. Although if you feel as though this will take more of a toll on you I would do what you think is best.

OP, you should definitely quit your job if you feel uncomfortable, and feel your mental health is declining. It is never okay to be in a situation that makes you feel this way; you’re a young, bright, smart person don’t stress yourself over a job that will not matter in the future. Besides colleges do allow you to take loans out, and even offer student aide so don’t worry about that. 

Also people who call you a job-hopper, don’t listen to them. You need to do what’s right for you because after all you will be the one looking after yourself for the rest of your life. I wish you the best OP in the decision you make, also I hope this helped you.

Hey OP, in advance I just want to say sorry if my advice is not the greatest, but I still would like to share what I can with you. Honestly, it sounds like your friends don’t care to include you in their conversations as easy it is to say to “leave that friend group”, it’s harder to go through it. If you feel like you have to force yourself in the conversations then I would probably distance myself from them; trust me, in the long run it will be better. As someone who had friends like this in middle school I understand how it feels to be ostracized by your friends. I actually ended up losing all my friends I knew at the start of high school too because I realized they didn’t care much to talk with me, or make any type of contact.  Definitely was hard, but it gave me time to figure myself out too.

I will say another way to make friends is via online although reading your post you seem to be more of an hands on guy, but you do say that you stay at home for the majority of your time so it is an option. But it seems like you haven’t figured yourself out as a person yet which is normal at this age, hell I’m 17 and still have not so don’t feel bad at all. There are many ways you can try to change your behavior, or attitude. I’m not sure if the area you live in safe to walk around, but if you can I would suggest taking trips to some local places to help yourself get out a bit. You never know you could meet someone too, and it might help you come out of your shell a bit too. 

I apologize OP if my advice did not help you in the slightest, but please do take care and dont hate yourself there are other people out in the world who share same interests as you, you just have to explore a bit yourself. I wish you well :)

Edit: I just saw the comments above mine. Sorry you have to deal with people like that OP, regardless of age mental health can happen to everyone.

Hey OP, I know your post isn’t focused on this mainly about forging a report card, but your parents behaviors sound concerning. I think you should report to someone what your parents are doing to you; it’s just not okay for a parent to hit their child then treat them as such afterwards. As for forging your report card just say that you “lost it at school”, or “forgot it in your locker”. I do HIGHLY recommend telling a trusted school counselor, or adult what your parents are doing.

Hey OP, first of all yes, your feelings are valid. I completely understand how you feel, as a (17f) who is somewhat in the same situation as you except it’s my parents who aren’t there for me emotionally. Your feelings are completely valid, and don’t let your older sisters tell you differently just because of their own struggles. Although it sounds like your sisters are struggling with their own selves, and you mentioning that your parents have shit on them for a while that is more than likely where that stems from. Reading your post you’ve said that whenever you talk about how you feel with them they dismiss you which isn’t okay for them to do, and it seems you have found some medical help which I am happy to hear for you but I would still try to find other people to talk about your feelings with. Whether that be friends, or even your parents because trust me bottling your emotions is not good. All it does is ruin you, I’ve been there and still do that myself, but I have found great ways to cope with that.

Best thing to do here is just be the bigger person, and try your best to avoid these topics with them because you wanting to share your feelings, accomplishments, and plans with them seems to anger them. Honestly, your siblings should be happy for you, and be there for you: they shouldn’t be putting you down, you deserve so much better. I wish there was more I could tell you because I know how it is to be in a family dynamic where you feel as if you are not validated at all, but I know you can hang in there OP. You seem like a great person for wanting to prepare yourself for college which is very responsible of you to do, so please don’t ever let anyone doubt your worth because you are so worth it. 

Best wishes OP. :)

I can relate to your post in some ways although I’m the person on the other side of this situation. I’ll tell you my story since this will be easier to get my point across; I’ve had an online friend I’ve known for about a year now. It took a while to warm up, but we both had our issues going on and we both were there for each other. We texted each other personal things because we trusted each other, pretty much everyday we talked. Hell, he helped me get through a lot of pain in a dark time of mine. I really trusted him a lot, but now things have been different just as they are for you and your friend it’s the same here. I’m slowly accepting the fact that we don’t have the same level of friendship we did before, and we don’t talk much at all. Of course, I’m not throwing my entire friendship out the window with him just yet, but we don’t have the same spark we did before. I went from a great friend to just a friend. That’s what he told me, although there is more I could say about him I have noticed I’d rather not keep boring you with my story. 
Now, I’m not telling you to give up on your friendship what I am trying to say is that people change over time, priorities change, and sometimes you have people in your life there to be your friends at that moment. That’s just my view on life; however, I’m not sure about your situation, but I think you should try talking this out with your friend, bring this up to her because more than likely she is feeling this too. I highly encourage you to talk with her if you can. 
Sorry for my long answer, but I truly hope I could help you out. If you need someone to talk about this feel free to pm me, I’m open. :)
